Pick the best hand, or the hands that tie for best, from a list of five-card poker hands.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/poker) (MIT). Listed under [Games & Simulation](/examples/?subject=games-and-simulation).

```nomi-run
// FILE: poker.nomi
//# Picks the best poker hands from a list of hands.

/// Why a hand cannot be scored.
pub enum Error {
    InvalidHand String
}

/// The hands of poker, weakest first, so the derived order ranks them.
enum Category {
    HighCard
    OnePair
    TwoPair
    ThreeOfAKind
    Straight
    Flush
    FullHouse
    FourOfAKind
    StraightFlush
}

derive Comparable for Category

/// How strong a hand is: its category, then the ranks that break a tie
/// within it, in the order they are compared. The derived order compares
/// the fields in the order they are declared.
struct Score {
    category: Category
    ranks: List<Int>
}

derive Comparable for Score

struct Card {
    rank: Int
    suit: String
}

/// The hands of `hands` that score highest, in the order given: one, or
/// every hand that ties for best.
pub fn best_hands(hands: List<String>) -> Result<List<String>, Error> {
    scored =
        hands
        |> Iter.map(fn hand -> Ok(#(hand, score(hand)?)))
        |> Result.collect()?

    Some(best) = scored |> Iter.map(.1) |> Iter.max() else { return Ok([]) }

    scored
    |> Iter.filter(fn #(_hand, score) -> score == best)
    |> Iter.map(.0)
    |> Iter.to_list()
    |> Ok()
}

/// The score of a hand of five cards written as `"4S 5S 7H 8D JC"`.
fn score(hand: String) -> Result<Score, Error> {
    Some(cards) = hand |> String.words() |> Iter.map(card) |> Maybe.collect() else {
        return Err(.InvalidHand(hand))
    }

    if Iter.count(cards) != 5 { return Err(.InvalidHand(hand)) }

    // Each rank with how many cards show it, the largest group first and
    // the higher rank first among groups of one size.
    groups =
        cards
        |> Iter.map(.rank)
        |> Iter.frequencies()
        |> Iter.sort_by(.Descending, fn #(rank, count) -> #(count, rank))

    counts = groups |> Iter.map(.1) |> Iter.to_list()
    ranks = groups |> Iter.map(.0) |> Iter.to_list()
    flush = cards |> Iter.map(.suit) |> Iter.to_set() |> Set.size() == 1

    Ok(
        case #(counts, straight(ranks), flush) {
            #([4, 1], _, _) -> #{category: .FourOfAKind, ranks}
            #([3, 2], _, _) -> #{category: .FullHouse, ranks}
            #([3, 1, 1], _, _) -> #{category: .ThreeOfAKind, ranks}
            #([2, 2, 1], _, _) -> #{category: .TwoPair, ranks}
            #([2, 1, 1, 1], _, _) -> #{category: .OnePair, ranks}
            #(_, Some(high), True) -> #{category: .StraightFlush, ranks: high}
            #(_, Some(high), False) -> #{category: .Straight, ranks: high}
            #(_, None, True) -> #{category: .Flush, ranks}
            #(_, None, False) -> #{category: .HighCard, ranks}
        }
    )
}

/// The ranks of a straight, highest first, when `ranks` (five different
/// ones, highest first) make one. An ace counts low in `A 2 3 4 5`.
fn straight(ranks: List<Int>) -> Maybe<List<Int>> {
    case ranks {
        [14, 5, 4, 3, 2] -> Some([5, 4, 3, 2, 1])
        [high, _, _, _, low] when high - low == 4 -> Some(ranks)
        _ -> None
    }
}

/// A card written as its rank and its suit, `"10H"` or `"QS"`.
fn card(text: String) -> Maybe<Card> {
    length = String.length(text)
    suit = String.drop(text, length - 1)

    if not List.contains(["S", "H", "D", "C"], suit) { return None }

    rank = case String.take(text, length - 1) {
        "J" -> Some(11)
        "Q" -> Some(12)
        "K" -> Some(13)
        "A" -> Some(14)
        digits -> pip_rank(digits)
    }

    Some(#Card{rank: rank?, suit})
}

/// The rank of a numbered card, 2 to 10.
fn pip_rank(digits: String) -> Maybe<Int> {
    Some(n) = String.to_int(digits) else { return None }

    if Range.contains(2..=10, n) {
        Some(n)
    } else {
        None
    }
}

// FILE: poker_test.nomi
import poker.{self, Error}

test "best hands" {
    cases = [
        #("single hand always wins", ["4S 5S 7H 8D JC"], ["4S 5S 7H 8D JC"]),
        #(
            "highest card out of all hands wins",
            ["4D 5S 6S 8D 3C", "2S 4C 7S 9H 10H", "3S 4S 5D 6H JH"],
            ["3S 4S 5D 6H JH"],
        ),
        #(
            "a tie has multiple winners",
            ["4D 5S 6S 8D 3C", "2S 4C 7S 9H 10H", "3S 4S 5D 6H JH", "3H 4H 5C 6C JD"],
            ["3S 4S 5D 6H JH", "3H 4H 5C 6C JD"],
        ),
        #(
            "multiple hands with the same high cards, tie compares next highest ranked, down to last card",
            ["3S 5H 6S 8D 7H", "2S 5D 6D 8C 7S"],
            ["3S 5H 6S 8D 7H"],
        ),
        #(
            "winning high card hand also has the lowest card",
            ["2S 5H 6S 8D 7H", "3S 4D 6D 8C 7S"],
            ["2S 5H 6S 8D 7H"],
        ),
        #("one pair beats high card", ["4S 5H 6C 8D KH", "2S 4H 6S 4D JH"], ["2S 4H 6S 4D JH"]),
        #("highest pair wins", ["4S 2H 6S 2D JH", "2S 4H 6C 4D JD"], ["2S 4H 6C 4D JD"]),
        #(
            "both hands have the same pair, high card wins",
            ["4H 4S AH JC 3D", "4C 4D AS 5D 6C"],
            ["4H 4S AH JC 3D"],
        ),
        #("two pairs beats one pair", ["2S 8H 6S 8D JH", "4S 5H 4C 8C 5C"], ["4S 5H 4C 8C 5C"]),
        #(
            "both hands have two pairs, highest ranked pair wins",
            ["2S 8H 2D 8D 3H", "4S 5H 4C 8S 5D"],
            ["2S 8H 2D 8D 3H"],
        ),
        #(
            "both hands have two pairs, with the same highest ranked pair, tie goes to low pair",
            ["2S QS 2C QD JH", "JD QH JS 8D QC"],
            ["JD QH JS 8D QC"],
        ),
        #(
            "both hands have two identically ranked pairs, tie goes to remaining card (kicker)",
            ["JD QH JS 8D QC", "JS QS JC 2D QD"],
            ["JD QH JS 8D QC"],
        ),
        #(
            "both hands have two pairs that add to the same value, win goes to highest pair",
            ["6S 6H 3S 3H AS", "7H 7S 2H 2S AC"],
            ["7H 7S 2H 2S AC"],
        ),
        #(
            "two pairs first ranked by largest pair",
            ["5C 2S 5S 4H 4C", "6S 2S 6H 7C 2C"],
            ["6S 2S 6H 7C 2C"],
        ),
        #(
            "three of a kind beats two pair",
            ["2S 8H 2H 8D JH", "4S 5H 4C 8S 4H"],
            ["4S 5H 4C 8S 4H"],
        ),
        #(
            "both hands have three of a kind, tie goes to highest ranked triplet",
            ["2S 2H 2C 8D JH", "4S AH AS 8C AD"],
            ["4S AH AS 8C AD"],
        ),
        #(
            "with multiple decks, two players can have same three of a kind, ties go to highest remaining cards",
            ["5S AH AS 7C AD", "4S AH AS 8C AD"],
            ["4S AH AS 8C AD"],
        ),
        #(
            "a straight beats three of a kind",
            ["4S 5H 4C 8D 4H", "3S 4D 2S 6D 5C"],
            ["3S 4D 2S 6D 5C"],
        ),
        #(
            "aces can end a straight (10 J Q K A)",
            ["4S 5H 4C 8D 4H", "10D JH QS KD AC"],
            ["10D JH QS KD AC"],
        ),
        #(
            "aces can start a straight (A 2 3 4 5)",
            ["4S 5H 4C 8D 4H", "4D AH 3S 2D 5C"],
            ["4D AH 3S 2D 5C"],
        ),
        #(
            "aces cannot be in the middle of a straight (Q K A 2 3)",
            ["2C 3D 7H 5H 2S", "QS KH AC 2D 3S"],
            ["2C 3D 7H 5H 2S"],
        ),
        #(
            "both hands with a straight, tie goes to highest ranked card",
            ["4S 6C 7S 8D 5H", "5S 7H 8S 9D 6H"],
            ["5S 7H 8S 9D 6H"],
        ),
        #(
            "even though an ace is usually high, a 5-high straight is the lowest-scoring straight",
            ["2H 3C 4D 5D 6H", "4S AH 3S 2D 5H"],
            ["2H 3C 4D 5D 6H"],
        ),
        #("flush beats a straight", ["4C 6H 7D 8D 5H", "2S 4S 5S 6S 7S"], ["2S 4S 5S 6S 7S"]),
        #(
            "both hands have a flush, tie goes to high card, down to the last one if necessary",
            ["2H 7H 8H 9H 6H", "3S 5S 6S 7S 8S"],
            ["2H 7H 8H 9H 6H"],
        ),
        #("full house beats a flush", ["3H 6H 7H 8H 5H", "4S 5H 4C 5D 4H"], ["4S 5H 4C 5D 4H"]),
        #(
            "both hands have a full house, tie goes to highest-ranked triplet",
            ["4H 4S 4D 9S 9D", "5H 5S 5D 8S 8D"],
            ["5H 5S 5D 8S 8D"],
        ),
        #(
            "with multiple decks, both hands have a full house with the same triplet, tie goes to the pair",
            ["5H 5S 5D 9S 9D", "5H 5S 5D 8S 8D"],
            ["5H 5S 5D 9S 9D"],
        ),
        #(
            "four of a kind beats a full house",
            ["4S 5H 4D 5D 4H", "3S 3H 2S 3D 3C"],
            ["3S 3H 2S 3D 3C"],
        ),
        #(
            "both hands have four of a kind, tie goes to high quad",
            ["2S 2H 2C 8D 2D", "4S 5H 5S 5D 5C"],
            ["4S 5H 5S 5D 5C"],
        ),
        #(
            "with multiple decks, both hands with identical four of a kind, tie determined by kicker",
            ["3S 3H 2S 3D 3C", "3S 3H 4S 3D 3C"],
            ["3S 3H 4S 3D 3C"],
        ),
        #(
            "straight flush beats four of a kind",
            ["4S 5H 5S 5D 5C", "7S 8S 9S 6S 10S"],
            ["7S 8S 9S 6S 10S"],
        ),
        #(
            "aces can end a straight flush (10 J Q K A)",
            ["KC AH AS AD AC", "10C JC QC KC AC"],
            ["10C JC QC KC AC"],
        ),
        #(
            "aces can start a straight flush (A 2 3 4 5)",
            ["KS AH AS AD AC", "4H AH 3H 2H 5H"],
            ["4H AH 3H 2H 5H"],
        ),
        #(
            "aces cannot be in the middle of a straight flush (Q K A 2 3)",
            ["2C AC QC 10C KC", "QH KH AH 2H 3H"],
            ["2C AC QC 10C KC"],
        ),
        #(
            "both hands have a straight flush, tie goes to highest-ranked card",
            ["4H 6H 7H 8H 5H", "5S 7S 8S 9S 6S"],
            ["5S 7S 8S 9S 6S"],
        ),
        #(
            "even though an ace is usually high, a 5-high straight flush is the lowest-scoring straight flush",
            ["2H 3H 4H 5H 6H", "4D AD 3D 2D 5D"],
            ["2H 3H 4H 5H 6H"],
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, hands, expected), description {
        assert poker.best_hands(hands) == Ok(expected)
    }
}

// Not a canonical case: the canonical hands are all well formed.
test "a hand with a card that is not a card is refused" {
    assert poker.best_hands(["4S 5S 7H 8D 1C"]) == Err(Error.InvalidHand("4S 5S 7H 8D 1C"))
    assert poker.best_hands(["4S 5S 7H 8D JX"]) == Err(Error.InvalidHand("4S 5S 7H 8D JX"))
    assert poker.best_hands(["4S 5S 7H 8D"]) == Err(Error.InvalidHand("4S 5S 7H 8D"))
}
```

## How it's written

- Each hand gets a `Score`: its `Category`, an enum of the nine hands from high card to straight flush, and the ranks that break a tie, in the order they are compared. Both derive `Comparable`, so the enum's declaration order ranks the categories and the struct compares category first, then the rank lists lexicographically. The best hands are those whose score equals `Iter.max` of the scores, kept in input order.
- The tie-break ranks come from one sort: each rank with how many cards show it, sorted descending by `#(count, rank)`. A full house `5 5 5 9 9` gives `[5, 9]`, two pairs `J Q J Q 8` give `[12, 11, 8]`, and a high-card hand its five ranks from the top, so every category compares its ranks the same way.
- The category is one `case` over the group counts, the straight and the flush together: `#([3, 2], _, _)` is a full house, `#(_, Some(high), True)` a straight flush. `straight` answers the straight's ranks, `[5, 4, 3, 2, 1]` for the wheel `A 2 3 4 5`, so a 5-high straight ranks below a 6-high one without a case of its own.
- The hands arrive as text, so a card that is not a card is data from outside: `best_hands` returns `Err(.InvalidHand(hand))` for it, or for a hand that is not five cards, rather than trapping. The canonical data has no such hand; the test file adds one test of three, marked as not canonical.
- The 37 current canonical cases are one `subtests` table named by the description column. Two cases that newer ones reimplement are left out: the first "two players can have same three of a kind" case and the first "both hands have a flush" case, whose newer versions use different hands.
